content: .{@-जम्, जन्मन्@} {%n.%} {@-रुहम्@} ({@सरोजम्, सरोजन्मन्, सरोरुहम्@}) also सरसिजम्, सरसिरुहम् a lotus; सरसिजमनुविद्धं शैवलेनापि रम्यम् <ls>Ś. 1. 20</ls>; [Shri Kṣītiśachandra Chatterji points out in Mañjūṣā (March, 1958) that the word सरसिजम् has been used in the sense of ‘a lotus’ probably for the first time by Kālidāsa. According to lexicographers the word सरसिज is met with first in the Suśruta Saṃhitā (1. 46. 124) as an adjective qualifying मत्स्याः. Bhāravi uses the word in the sense of ‘a land lotus’ in उत्फुल्लस्थलनलिनीवनादमुष्मादुद्धूतः सरसिजसंभवः परागः. Three stages of being यौगिक, योगरूढ and रूढ are thus clearly seen in the history of the word.]; सरोरुहद्युतिमुषः पादांस्तवासेवितुम् <ls>Ratn. 1. 30</ls>.
